Exercise: Reverse Cable Curl

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
isolation

Force Type:
pull

Difficulty Level:
beginner

Movement Patterns:

- elbow_flexion

Primary Muscles:

- biceps

Secondary Muscles:

- forearms

Equipment:

- cable

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
2.5

Energy Requirement:
moderate

Recovery Time:
1 hours

Goals:

- bicep_hypertrophy
- forearm_strength

Contraindications:

- Hypertension patients should avoid this exercise due to potential strain on the cardiovascular system.
- Individuals with a history of biceps tendonitis or elbow injuries should use caution and possibly seek medical advice before performing this exercise.

Exercise Variations:

- name: Concentration Curl, instructions: ['Sit on a bench with your back against it and hold a dumbbell in one hand. Place the same-side knee on top of the bench to support your arm.']
- name: Hammer Curl, instructions: ['Hold two dumbbells with palms facing each other, then perform the curl while keeping the forearms parallel to the floor throughout the movement.']

Substitution Options:

- exercise_name: Barbell Curl, equipment: barbell
- exercise_name: Dumbbell Curl, equipment: dumbbells

Instructions:

- Stand up with your torso upright while holding a bar attachment that is attached to a low pulley using a pronated (palms down) and shoulder width grip. Make sure also that you keep the elbows close to the torso. This will be your starting position.
- While holding the upper arms stationary, curl the weights while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Only the forearms should move. Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the muscle.
- Slowly begin to bring the bar back to starting position as your breathe in.
- Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
